answer: The protocol enforces sybil resistance by requiring 4,000 megabytes of memory-hard work per agent, gating each identity through a unique data structure challenge. The verifier monitors an inlet for incoming tasks, assigning each to a non-overlapping memory block carved into a marble-like grid. An honest participant pays for one unit of memory-hard work, while 1,000 fakes incur 1,000 times that cost, as each requires a distinct onyx memory footprint to pass verification. Any evidence of memory-sharing triggers an immediate, permanent lockout of all colluding identities.
